messages:
Lina: FYI I ran the v5-ptq bringup on the eval holdout. NDCG@10 +0.9% but MRR@1 down -3.7%. Posting quick triage notes.

Omar: curious — same candidate pool and same preproc? small tokenization diffs can nuke head.

Lina: candidate pool identical. Eval harness used a dev-normalizer that preserves brackets; prod strips them. Token counts dev=22, prod=20.

Dan: that could shift which candidate occupies #1. Also check quant calibration — did you use global min-max or per-channel?

Lina: per-channel weights, activations PTQ using global min-max with clipping at 99.5 percentile.

Omar: two experiments: 1) re-run with prod normalizer 2) recalibrate activations using stratified sampling including short queries.

Lina: kicked both off. qa-bot: job_362001 started (Lina)  re-eval with prod-normalizer + stratified-calib.

Dan: also compute score spread (p1,p50,p99) for float vs ptq. If spread collapses, head volatility explains MRR drop.

Lina: float p1=-0.55 p50=0.11 p99=1.43; ptq p1=-0.09 p50=0.07 p99=0.88 -> collapsed.

Omar: agreed. If normalization fixed tokenization, and stratified calib restores tails, should recover MRR. Try asymmetric activation quant as well.

Lina: results: with prod-normalizer + stratified calibrator + asymmetric-acts, MRR@1 now -0.3%, NDCG@10 +0.8%. Good.

Dan: would like a small onboarding test: after quant, assert (p99-p1)_ptq >= 0.6*(p99-p1)_float or else block. Saves future surprises. Created ticket INF-1450.

Omar: add model-card note: "Quant notes: activations=asymmetric, calib=stratified (short/med/long), post-quant-range-check INF-1450"

Lina: will update card and push canary. Closing unless new regressions. :white_check_mark:
